section: Indian Independence Act 1947; the Constituent Assembly - demand, composition, functioning
subsections: Sessions and dates - first meeting, Objectives Resolution, adoption, signing, final session, time taken

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the opening of the Constituent Assembly:
1. The first meeting was attended by 211 members.
2. The Muslim League boycotted the first meeting.
3. Dr Rajendra Prasad was elected President at the first meeting itself.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The first meeting was attended by 211 members, while the Muslim League boycotted it. Dr Rajendra Prasad was elected President on 11 December 1946, not at the first meeting.
accepted.tq: Find the incorrect statement by checking the precise sequence of events and dates.
accepted.sec: Sessions and dates - first meeting, Objectives Resolution, adoption, signing, final session, time taken

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Publication of the Draft Constitution
B. Adoption of the Objectives Resolution
C. Beginning of the third reading of the Constitution
D. Setting up of the Drafting Committee
accepted.x: The Objectives Resolution was adopted on 22 January 1947, the Drafting Committee was set up on 29 August 1947, the Draft Constitution was published on 21 February 1948, and the third reading began on 14 November 1949.
accepted.tq: Place the earliest dated event first and then verify the middle sequence.
accepted.sec: Sessions and dates - first meeting, Objectives Resolution, adoption, signing, final session, time taken

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below:

List-I (Date)
A. 11 December 1946
B. 22 January 1947
C. 17 November 1947
D. 21 February 1948

List-II (Event)
1. Draft Constitution published
2. Rajendra Prasad elected President
3. Constituent Assembly met as Dominion Legislature
4. Objectives Resolution adopted
accepted.x: Rajendra Prasad was elected President on 11 December 1946; the Objectives Resolution was adopted on 22 January 1947; the Assembly met as Dominion Legislature on 17 November 1947; and the Draft Constitution was published on 21 February 1948.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure date-event pair and eliminate codes that disturb the sequence.

accepted.s:
With reference to the Constituent Assembly, consider the following statements:
1. Dr Rajendra Prasad was elected President on 11 December 1946.
2. H.C. Mukherjee was its Vice-President.
3. B.N. Rau served as its Constitutional Adviser.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Rajendra Prasad became President, H.C. Mukherjee was Vice-President, and B.N. Rau served as Constitutional Adviser.
accepted.tq: Test a cluster of related office-holders without confusing elected posts with advisory positions.
accepted.sec: Sessions and dates - first meeting, Objectives Resolution, adoption, signing, final session, time taken

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the working of the Constituent Assembly?
o: It held 11 sessions and sat for 165 days over exactly three years.
It held 9 sessions and sat for 165 days over 2 years, 11 months and 18 days.
It held 12 sessions and sat for 165 days over 2 years, 11 months and 18 days.
It held 11 sessions and sat for 165 days over 2 years, 11 months and 18 days.
accepted.x: The Constituent Assembly held 11 sessions and had 165 days of sittings over 2 years, 11 months and 18 days, approximately three years.
accepted.tq: Check each numerical component separately rather than relying on the approximate figure alone.
accepted.sec: Sessions and dates - first meeting, Objectives Resolution, adoption, signing, final session, time taken

accepted.s: The approximate cost incurred in framing the Constitution of India was:
accepted.x: The Constituent Assembly incurred an approximate expenditure of Rs 64 lakh in framing the Constitution.
accepted.tq: Use the exact quantitative figure and reject nearby numerical distractors.
accepted.sec: Sessions and dates - first meeting, Objectives Resolution, adoption, signing, final session, time taken

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs correctly represents the amendments proposed and discussed during the framing of the Constitution?
accepted.x: A total of 7,635 amendments were proposed, of which 2,473 were discussed. The figures 7,653 and 3,473 do not represent the stated totals.
accepted.tq: Compare both figures in a paired numerical fact instead of identifying only one number.
accepted.sec: Sessions and dates - first meeting, Objectives Resolution, adoption, signing, final session, time taken

accepted.s: As adopted, the Constitution of India contained:
accepted.x: The Constitution, as adopted, consisted of 395 Articles, 22 Parts and 8 Schedules.
accepted.tq: Test the original constitutional structure through a precise three-part numerical combination.
accepted.sec: Sessions and dates - first meeting, Objectives Resolution, adoption, signing, final session, time taken

accepted.s: Which of the following groups of provisions came into force on 26 November 1949 along with the adoption of the Constitution?
o: All provisions relating exclusively to State governments
Emergency provisions, Union Territories and official language provisions only
Citizenship, elections, provisional Parliament and transitional provisions
Fundamental Rights, Directive Principles and Fundamental Duties only
accepted.x: Citizenship, elections, the provisional Parliament and transitional provisions came into force on 26 November 1949. The remaining constitutional provisions generally commenced on 26 January 1950.
accepted.tq: Identify the special early-commencement provisions rather than applying the general commencement date.
accepted.sec: Sessions and dates - first meeting, Objectives Resolution, adoption, signing, final session, time taken

accepted.s: Which one of the following Articles was NOT included among the provisions that came into force on 26 November 1949?
accepted.x: Articles 5, 60 and 324 were among the provisions that came into force on 26 November 1949. Article 32 was not included in that specified group of early-commencement provisions.
accepted.tq: Find the one Article outside the specifically listed early-commencement provisions.
accepted.sec: Sessions and dates - first meeting, Objectives Resolution, adoption, signing, final session, time taken

accepted.s: The representatives of which of the following groups of princely States joined the Constituent Assembly on 28 April 1947?
o: Baroda, Bikaner, Kashmir, Patiala, Travancore and Udaipur
Baroda, Bikaner, Jaipur, Patiala, Rewa and Udaipur
Bikaner, Gwalior, Jaipur, Mysore, Rewa and Udaipur
Baroda, Bhopal, Jaipur, Patiala, Rewa and Hyderabad
accepted.x: Representatives of six princely States—Baroda, Bikaner, Jaipur, Patiala, Rewa and Udaipur—joined the Constituent Assembly on 28 April 1947.
accepted.tq: Use the complete membership list to eliminate options containing substituted princely States.
accepted.sec: Sessions and dates - first meeting, Objectives Resolution, adoption, signing, final session, time taken

accepted.s: When the Constituent Assembly met as the Dominion Legislature, who was elected its Speaker?
accepted.x: The Constituent Assembly met as the Dominion Legislature on 17 November 1947, when G.V. Mavalankar was elected Speaker.
accepted.tq: Match the office-holder with the specific institutional phase in which the office was held.
accepted.sec: Sessions and dates - first meeting, Objectives Resolution, adoption, signing, final session, time taken

accepted.s: The final session of the Constituent Assembly was held on 24 January 1950. Which important event is associated with this sitting?
o: The Objectives Resolution was moved by Jawaharlal Nehru.
The Assembly first met as the Dominion Legislature.
accepted.x: The final session was held on 24 January 1950, when members signed the Constitution. The Objectives Resolution was moved earlier, the Drafting Committee was set up in 1947, and the Dominion Legislature phase began in November 1947.
accepted.tq: Associate the final session with its defining event while rejecting earlier milestones.
accepted.sec: Sessions and dates - first meeting, Objectives Resolution, adoption, signing, final session, time taken

accepted.s: Out of the 299 members of the Constituent Assembly, how many signed the Constitution?
accepted.x: The Constitution was signed by 284 of the 299 members of the Constituent Assembly.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the total membership from the number of members who actually signed.
accepted.sec: Sessions and dates - first meeting, Objectives Resolution, adoption, signing, final session, time taken

accepted.s: The Constitution of India came into force on 26 January 1950 because this date was associated with:
o: The Purna Swaraj declaration associated with the Lahore Congress of 1929
The first meeting of the Constituent Assembly in 1946
The adoption of the Objectives Resolution in 1947
The publication of the Draft Constitution in 1948
accepted.x: 26 January was chosen to commemorate Purna Swaraj Day, following the Lahore Congress decision of 1929 and its observance in 1930.
accepted.tq: Link a constitutional date with its historical nationalist significance.
accepted.sec: Sessions and dates - first meeting, Objectives Resolution, adoption, signing, final session, time taken

accepted.s: Constitution Day, or Samvidhan Divas, is observed in India on:
accepted.x: Constitution Day is observed on 26 November, the date on which the Constitution was adopted. The observance has been in effect since 2015, the year of the 125th birth anniversary of Dr B.R. Ambedkar.
accepted.tq: Separate the adoption date and Constitution Day from the commencement date.
accepted.sec: Sessions and dates - first meeting, Objectives Resolution, adoption, signing, final session, time taken

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the sequence relating to the provisional Parliament?
o: It ceased in April 1952, and the new Parliament was constituted in May 1952.
It ceased in January 1950, and the new Parliament was constituted in April 1952.
It ceased in May 1952, and the new Parliament was constituted in April 1952.
It ceased in November 1949, and the new Parliament was constituted in January 1950.
accepted.x: The provisional Parliament ceased to function on 17 April 1952, and the new Parliament came into existence in May 1952.
accepted.tq: Track the institutional transition by identifying the ending date before the succeeding arrangement.
